text:
olivia: RFC follow-up: can we pack microwindows by cost-quantile instead of tokens? goal: fewer stragglers without blocking tiny cheap requests. quick thoughts?
ryan: sounds promising. map each request -> cost_score -> quantile q, only coalesce same q in a microwindow. cheap to compute if thresholds preloaded.
leah: downside: if many requests land in high-q, we could underutilize. need sim to pick N quantiles per model.
matt: runtime constraints: admission <300us. keep mapping O(1) (floor(score/step) or tiny LUT). store thresholds in shared mem.
maya: observability: log assigned_quantile, estimated_compute, actual_compute; expose residual histogram per model-version. auto-tune thresholds if residual drift >25%.
canarybot: :white_check_mark: quantile_canary started on runtime-canary-2 sampling=2%
ryan: also propose per-tenant soft-credits: deduct estimated_cost at enqueue, reject or fallback if negative. prevents noisy tenants hogging headroom.
leah: soft-evict sketch: if actual compute exceeds budget, mark batch overflow, slice trailing slots or route to emergency fastpath. emit metadata evicted_by=soft-evict.
matt: unit tests + sim: I'll build a tiny sim with bimodal cost profiles to measure p99 improvement vs throughput loss.
olivia: action items: ryan -> sim + N suggestions; leah -> soft-evict doc + hold-time per quantile; maya -> metrics + dashboards; matt -> shared-mem layout. reconvene with numbers tomorrow. :coffee:
